citation: Mishra R., Gupta D., Marathe A., Yu K. D., Schroeder A., Swarup S. (2026) Estimating the cascading global impacts of gas disruptions in Qatar. arXiv:2604.24960

dedupe_keys.name: multiregional input output model of the cascading global impacts of a gas supply disruption in qatar 2026

description: This model estimates the global knock-on effects of a local disruption of Qatar's gas sector with a multiregional input-output framework and scenario analysis. It asks whether trade reallocation and higher production elsewhere can offset the loss, and finds large gas supply losses in Asia and Europe, with the largest aggregate impacts in India, China and South Korea; trade reallocation mitigates part of the loss, and more production by major gas producers helps, but benefits stay concentrated in a few large economies and give little relief to countries such as India and Pakistan. It was developed by Ritwick Mishra, Diksha Gupta, Achla Marathe, Krista Danielle Yu, Aaron Schroeder and Samarth Swarup and posted on arXiv on 27 April 2026. Coverage is global. The preprint is available free online; only the arXiv licence link is shown and no code or data are linked. Caveats: it is a preprint, input-output models assume fixed production recipes in the short run, and the full text was not read. For simulation it traces how a gas shock propagates to industries that use gas as fuel and feedstock, such as chemicals and fertilisers, useful for cross-border supply chain resilience scenarios. It is related to the EXIOBASE multiregional input-output database record in this catalogue.
